Why_Consider: Early personality or behavioral change with executive dysfunction may be more suggestive of FTD than typical amnestic AD.
Distinguishing_Features: Early disinhibition, loss of empathy, compulsive behavior, prominent executive dysfunction
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Early behavioral/language symptoms dominate while episodic memory may be relatively preserved initially.
Red_Flag_Features: Early severe behavior change; disinhibition; loss of empathy; compulsive behavior
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Detailed neuropsychological assessment plus MRI focused on frontal/anterior temporal patterns

Why_Consider: Hallucinations and attention fluctuation can point away from typical AD and toward Lewy body disease.
Distinguishing_Features: Visual hallucinations, cognitive fluctuation, parkinsonism, REM sleep behavior disorder
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Visual hallucinations, cognitive fluctuations, parkinsonism, or REM sleep behavior disorder are more prominent than typical AD.

Suggested_Next_Assessment: Clinical evaluation for parkinsonism/fluctuation plus structural imaging if needed

Why_Consider: Executive dysfunction with stepwise or focal features should prompt vascular evaluation.
Distinguishing_Features: Stepwise decline, focal neurologic signs, vascular lesions on MRI
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Stepwise decline, focal neurologic signs, and vascular brain injury support vascular cognitive disorder.
Red_Flag_Features: Stepwise decline; focal deficits; gait disorder; vascular lesions on imaging
Suggested_Next_Assessment: MRI for vascular burden and neurologic examination for focal signs
Reference: Sachdev P. Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement. Alzheimer Disease and Associated Disorders. 2014;28(3):206-218. DOI: 10.1097/WAD.0000000000000034. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24632990/
AD_vs_Other_Core_Difference: Stepwise decline, focal neurologic signs, and vascular brain injury support vascular cognitive disorder.
Recommended_Discrimination_Assessment: MRI for vascular burden and neurologic examination for focal signs
Chinese_Distinguishing_Features: 常见阶梯样进展、局灶神经系统体征或影像学血管性病变证据。

Why_Consider: Depression can cause cognitive complaints and mimic early AD; mood symptoms require assessment.
Distinguishing_Features: Prominent low mood, sleep/appetite change, variable effort, improvement with mood treatment
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Mood symptoms, sleep/appetite changes, and variable effort can dominate the cognitive complaint.
Red_Flag_Features: Prominent low mood; anhedonia; sleep disturbance; inconsistent cognitive effort
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Mood assessment plus cognitive reassessment after addressing reversible contributors
Reference: Arvanitakis Z. Diagnosis and Management of Dementia: Review. JAMA. 2019;322(16):1589-1599. DOI: 10.1001/jama.2019.4782. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31638686/

Why_Consider: Acute or fluctuating attention disturbance is not typical for gradual AD onset.
Distinguishing_Features: Acute onset, fluctuation, altered arousal, medical trigger or medication effect
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Acute onset and fluctuating attention/arousal are not typical for gradual AD presentation.
Red_Flag_Features: Acute onset; fluctuating consciousness; medical trigger; medication toxicity
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Urgent medical evaluation for delirium causes plus medication and laboratory review
Reference: Inouye SK. Delirium in elderly people. Lancet. 2014;383(9920):911-922. DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60688-1. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23992774/
AD_vs_Other_Core_Difference: Acute onset and fluctuating attention/arousal are not typical for gradual AD presentation.
Recommended_Discrimination_Assessment: Urgent medical evaluation for delirium causes plus medication and laboratory review
Chinese_Distinguishing_Features: 起病急、注意和意识水平波动明显，常存在感染、代谢紊乱或药物等诱因。

Why_Consider: Language-predominant symptoms can be AD-compatible but require PPA and FTD differential assessment.
Distinguishing_Features: Prominent aphasia, naming/comprehension profile, anterior temporal or frontal involvement
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Language syndrome is dominant and may follow PPA patterns rather than typical memory-predominant AD.
Red_Flag_Features: Early prominent aphasia; grammar or semantic impairment; asymmetric language-network atrophy
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Speech-language/neuropsychological assessment plus MRI and specialist evaluation
Reference: Gorno-Tempini ML. Classification of primary progressive aphasia and its variants. Neurology. 2011;76(11):1006-1014. DOI: 10.1212/WNL.0b013e31821103e6. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21325651/
AD_vs_Other_Core_Difference: Language syndrome is dominant and may follow PPA patterns rather than typical memory-predominant AD.
Recommended_Discrimination_Assessment: Speech-language/neuropsychological assessment plus MRI and specialist evaluation

Why_Consider: Psychosis can occur in AD but should trigger broader differential review.

AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Visual hallucinations, cognitive fluctuations, parkinsonism, or REM sleep behavior disorder are more prominent than typical AD.

Suggested_Next_Assessment: Clinical evaluation for parkinsonism/fluctuation plus structural imaging if needed

Clinical_Feature_Pattern: Functional decline without clear cognitive-domain impairment
Alternative_Diagnosis: Medical frailty or depression-related functional impairment
Why_Consider: Functional problems without objective cognitive-domain impairment may reflect non-AD causes.
Distinguishing_Features: Physical illness, sensory impairment, low mood, pain, medication burden
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Pattern differs from typical memory-predominant AD.
Red_Flag_Features: Rapid progression; early motor signs; atypical focal neurologic signs
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Detailed clinical review, neuropsychological assessment, and MRI

AD_vs_Other_Core_Difference: Pattern differs from typical memory-predominant AD.
Recommended_Discrimination_Assessment: Detailed clinical review, neuropsychological assessment, and MRI

Alternative_Diagnosis: Posterior cortical atrophy / ophthalmologic disease / Lewy body disease
Why_Consider: PCA is often AD-related but visual and Lewy body differentials remain important.
Distinguishing_Features: Early visual-perceptual complaints, reading difficulty, object localization problems
AD_vs_Other_Key_Difference: Visual-perceptual symptoms dominate and may reflect PCA, eye disease, or Lewy body disease.
Red_Flag_Features: Early visual-perceptual symptoms; hallucination; ocular disease; marked visuospatial dysfunction
Suggested_Next_Assessment: Visual assessment, neuropsychological visuospatial testing, and MRI
